video.transcriptSummary: This walkthrough follows the real six-stage Vibe Website Factory build for The Herd of Ibiza: GT-Alpaca. You will see how workspace bootstrap and grounded source research prevent made-up claims and catch critical dependency vulnerabilities early, how three-layer W3C design tokens enforce WCAG 2.1 AA contrast at compile time, how zero-native-binary GLB compression cuts a 4.52 megabyte 3D alpaca model down to 852 kilobytes, how five server-rendered routes stay readable to Google, Gemini, ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Claude, and how decoupled verification plus human-approved launch produce an honest numbered Proof Pack from 01 through 09.

steps.title: Bootstrap, Grounded Research & Creative Brief (Stages 0–1)
steps.summary: Every Vibe Website Factory build starts with zero guesswork: `cf-bootstrap` initializes `.memory/` and `plans/`, `cf-research` grounds every product number directly from primary repos (zero fabricated claims), `cf-grill-me` resolves creative trade-offs upfront, and `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` blocks vulnerable dependencies before a single page renders.

eli5.plainTitle: Set Up Your Workshop & Gather Real Facts First
eli5.oneLineHook: Never invent fake numbers or jump straight into layout—set up clean folders, verify real facts, and screen tools for safety first.
eli5.everydayAnalogy: A chef wiping down the counter, checking every ingredient label for freshness, and reading the recipe before turning on the stove.
eli5.simpleExplanation: Before designing a single button on a website, the Website Factory sets up a tidy project binder and collects only real, verified facts from your actual product files. For the GT-Alpaca website, we confirmed exact counts—twenty-two alpacas, seven Ibiza routes, twenty-three songs, and one heavy 3D sculpture—instead of guessing. We also scanned every software tool for license safety and security holes, catching three serious warnings right away and fixing them before coding.
eli5.whyItMatters: Websites built from vague prompts quickly fill up with made-up testimonials, mismatched stats, and unsafe third-party packages. Catching bad dependencies and fuzzy requirements on day one saves days of painful rework later.
eli5.roleInProtocol: This pairs Stages 0 and 1 of `cf-website-factory` (`cf-bootstrap`, `cf-research`, and `cf-grill-me`), creating Proof #01 (clean workspace tree) and Proof #02 (grounded facts, license compliance, and zero High/Critical CVEs).
eli5.howToUseGoingForward: Start every new website project by bootstrapping `.memory/`, listing your verified product facts in one research sheet, answering 5 Creative Brief questions, and confirming `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` exits cleanly with zero High or Critical issues.
eli5.whenToUse: Run Stages 0 and 1 at the very beginning of every website build—before picking colors, generating components, or installing UI libraries.
eli5.realWorldExample: On `gt-alpaca-website`, Proof #02 grounded 22 alpacas, 7 Ibiza routes, 23 audio tracks, and the raw 4.52 MB `avalon_poc.glb` directly from `herd_and_co`, excluded an MPL-2.0 library, and upgraded `vitest` from 3.2.4 to 5.1.2 to clear 3 Critical CVEs.
eli5.audioScript: Think of building a great website like cooking a big celebratory dinner. You would never toss mystery jars into a hot pan without checking expiration dates first. Stages zero and one of the Vibe Website Factory prepare your clean workshop before a single line of page code exists. First, bootstrap creates your project memory binder and proof folder. Next, grounded research pulls only real numbers straight from your product files, with zero made-up quotes or fake statistics. For the GT-Alpaca site, we verified twenty-two real alpacas, seven Ibiza routes, twenty-three original audio tracks, and a four-point-five-two megabyte three-D model. Best of all, our upfront security audit caught three critical package vulnerabilities in an older test runner and upgraded it immediately so the build began completely clean.
eli5.diagramCaption: How Stages 0–1 turn raw product repos into a clean workspace, verified fact sheet, license check, and zero-CVE foundation.

keyTakeaways: Proof #01 (`cf-bootstrap`): Creates `.memory/`, `plans/`, `.memory/feature-map.md`, `.agents/rules/`, and `proof-pack/` before any framework files are written.

Zero Fabricated Claims (`cf-research`): Every stat on `gt-alpaca-website` (`22` alpacas, `7` Ibiza routes, `23` tracks, `45s` `60fps` trailer, `4.52 MB` raw `avalon_poc.glb`) traces directly to `herd_and_co`, `product-video-studio`, and `Project_herd_and_co`.

License & CVE Hygiene: Verified 100% MIT / ISC / Apache-2.0 runtime and dev packages (excluding MPL-2.0 `@axe-core/playwright`) and upgraded `vitest@3.2.4` -> `5.1.2` after `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` caught `3` Critical CVEs.
Creative Brief Lock (`cf-grill-me`): Resolves palette polarity, 50% Hero anchor, target audiences, and commercial goals before touching design tokens or components.
actionChecklist: Run `cf-bootstrap` on a new website repo and add `.tmp/` to `.gitignore` so temporary screenshots stay untracked.
Record only verified source facts in `.memory/research.md` and save the bootstrap tree to `proof-pack/01-bootstrap.txt`.
Run `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` right after dependency selection and resolve every High/Critical CVE before Stage 2.

steps.title: 3-Layer W3C Design Tokens & Build-Time WCAG >= 4.5:1 (Stage 2A)
steps.summary: Eliminate generic AI-slop styling and contrast failures by authoring a single 3-layer W3C `design/tokens.json` (`primitive` -> `semantic` -> `component` + `dark.semantic`), compiling it into Tailwind CSS v4 `@theme inline` via `generate-tokens.mjs` with build-time WCAG 2.1 AA (`>= 4.5:1`) enforcement, and blocking raw `#hex` or arbitrary spacing literals with `validate-tokens.mjs`.

eli5.plainTitle: Build a Smart Color & Spacing Book That Checks Readability Automatically
eli5.oneLineHook: Define every brand color and spacing rule once in a master swatch book that refuses to build if text is too faint to read.
eli5.everydayAnalogy: An architect's paint-and-fabric sample binder with a built-in light meter that buzzes if wall lettering is too hard to see.
eli5.simpleExplanation: Instead of sprinkling random color codes across dozens of webpage files, we put every color, font, and spacing value into one neat three-layer swatch file. Layer one lists raw shades, layer two gives each shade a clear job like page background or button text, and layer three sets rules for cards and buttons plus dark mode. When we compile that file, a built-in readability check verifies every text-and-background pair passes eye-strain standards automatically.
eli5.whyItMatters: Hardcoded colors drift across pages, break dark mode, and leave low-contrast gray text that people on bright phone screens cannot read. Compiling tokens with automatic contrast checks stops visual mess and accessibility bugs at the factory door.
eli5.roleInProtocol: This is Stage 2A (`cf-design-tokens`): `generate-tokens.mjs` compiles `design/tokens.json` into `src/styles/tokens.css` (enforcing `>= 4.5:1` contrast and safe CSS values), while `validate-tokens.mjs` scans `src/` to reject raw `#hex` or `p-[19px]` hacks.
eli5.howToUseGoingForward: Create `design/tokens.json` before writing UI components, compile it into Tailwind CSS v4 `@theme inline`, name semantic tokens by purpose (`surface`, `foreground`, `primary`) rather than hue, and run `validate-tokens.mjs` in CI.
eli5.whenToUse: Use `cf-design-tokens` on every new website or design-system refresh right after locking your Creative Brief—and re-run `validate-tokens.mjs` after every UI edit.
eli5.realWorldExample: On `gt-alpaca-website`, Pass 1 `cf-reviewer` caught dark Espresso fill tokens used as text ink (`1.52:1–3.65:1`); adding dedicated `primary-text`/`accent-text`/`secondary-text` aliases expanded `design/tokens.json` to `40` primitive, `24` semantic, `6` component, and `19` dark overrides—passing `30/30` Light+Dark pairs (`>= 5.75:1` Light, `>= 7.62:1` Dark) with `0` literal violations.
eli5.audioScript: Imagine painting a whole house by mixing a slightly different shade of cream in every single room. By the time you reach the hallway, nothing matches. Design tokens fix that forever. In Stage two A, we organize every brand color, font size, and spacing step into one three-layer swatch file. The first layer holds raw palette colors, the second layer names them by job like background or readable text ink, and the third layer wires buttons, cards, and dark mode overrides. When our compiler builds Tailwind CSS variables, it checks text contrast automatically. On the GT-Alpaca site, our independent reviewer even caught dark mode text contrast gaps on pass one—so we added dedicated high-contrast text tokens and passed all thirty light and dark pairs cleanly.
eli5.diagramCaption: How 3-layer W3C tokens flow from primitive shades to semantic intent, dark overrides, 30-pair Light+Dark WCAG contrast math, and Tailwind v4 CSS.

keyTakeaways: 3-Layer W3C Hierarchy: Separate `primitive` (raw values), `semantic` (intent-named aliases like `primary-text` and `foreground`, never `blue-500`), `component` (`button.*`, `card.*`), and `dark.semantic` overrides.

Build-Time Accessibility & Safety: `generate-tokens.mjs` fails with exit `1` on cyclic `{ref}` chains, unsafe CSS injection strings (`</style`, `javascript:`), or any paired foreground/background ratio below `4.5:1`.

GT-Alpaca Verified Pass 2 Compilation: `40` primitive, `24` semantic, `6` component, and `19` dark overrides compiled to `src/styles/tokens.css` (`tailwind-v4`), closing Pass 1's dark-ink blocker to pass `30/30` Light+Dark WCAG pairs (`5.75:1–17.28:1` Light; `7.62:1–17.13:1` Dark) with `0` literal violations across `27` files.

Zero-Drift Source Guard: `validate-tokens.mjs --dir src/` blocks raw `#hex`, `rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsl()`, and arbitrary Tailwind brackets (`bg-[#...]`, `p-[19px]`), permitting `// @tokens-ignore-file` only for pure 3D material registries.
actionChecklist: Author `design/tokens.json` using `skills/cf-design-tokens/resources/tokens.template.json` as your starter structure.
Compile tokens with `generate-tokens.mjs --format tailwind-v4` and confirm every semantic foreground/background pair passes `>= 4.5:1`.
Run `validate-tokens.mjs --dir src/` before every commit to prove zero hardcoded color or pixel hacks crept into components.

codeSnippet.filename: Stage 2A Token Compile & Literal Scan Commands
codeSnippet.code:
# 1. Compile 3-layer W3C tokens -> Tailwind v4 @theme inline + WCAG >= 4.5:1 gate
node skills/cf-design-tokens/scripts/generate-tokens.mjs \
  --config design/tokens.json \
  --out src/styles/tokens.css \
  --format tailwind-v4

# 2. Enforce zero raw #hex / rgb() / arbitrary Tailwind brackets in src/
node skills/cf-design-tokens/scripts/validate-tokens.mjs --dir src/

steps.title: Zero-Native-Binary GLB Compression & Mobile 3D Craft (Stage 2B)
steps.summary: Ship 60 FPS interactive Three.js / React Three Fiber scenes without punishing mobile users: compress raw `.glb` models with `optimize-glb.mjs` (Meshopt + `KHR_mesh_quantization` + 1024px WebP via pure-JS `@gltf-transform/cli`), enforce `Timer`, `<PerformanceMonitor>`, capped DPR, and static fallbacks, and verify zero 3D anti-patterns with `audit-threejs.mjs`.

eli5.plainTitle: Shrink Giant 3D Models by 81% So Phones Stay Smooth and Cool
eli5.oneLineHook: Pack heavy 3D studio sculptures into featherweight web files and add smart safety guards so older phones never stutter or overheat.
eli5.everydayAnalogy: Vacuum-sealing a giant winter coat into a tiny carry-on pouch while keeping it fluffy and warm the moment you unpack it.
eli5.simpleExplanation: Raw 3D art straight from a studio is huge—on GT-Alpaca, our hero alpaca model started at over four and a half megabytes, which crawls on phones. Our zero-setup optimizer trims hidden parts, packs geometry tightly, and converts textures to WebP, shrinking it by over eighty-one percent to under one megabyte! Then our 3D rules keep frames smooth, cap screen workload, and swap in a crisp still picture if someone prefers reduced motion.
eli5.whyItMatters: Uncompressed 3D scenes freeze mobile browsers, drain batteries, and hurt search rankings. Shrinking models upfront and blocking slow per-frame mistakes gives every visitor an unforgettable hero without sacrificing speed.
eli5.roleInProtocol: This is Stage 2B (`cf-threejs-craft`), grounding Utsubo's 100 Three.js Performance Tips into two deterministic scripts: `optimize-glb.mjs` (zero native C++ tools required) and `audit-threejs.mjs` (blocking `setState` or `new THREE.*` inside `useFrame`, deprecated `THREE.Clock`, uncapped DPR, and unguarded `lil-gui`).
eli5.howToUseGoingForward: Run `optimize-glb.mjs` on every `.glb` before placing it in `public/models/`, wrap R3F scenes in `<PerformanceMonitor>` with DPR clamped to `2`, keep `lil-gui`/`stats-gl` dev-only, always supply a static WebP fallback, and pass `audit-threejs.mjs`.
eli5.whenToUse: Apply `cf-threejs-craft` anytime a site features an interactive 3D hero, product viewer, or WebGL canvas—especially when mobile visitors and Core Web Vitals matter.
eli5.realWorldExample: On `gt-alpaca-website`, `optimize-glb.mjs` shrank `avalon_poc.glb` from `4,736,680 B` (`4.52 MB`) down to `872,868 B` (`852 KB`)—an exact `81.57%` reduction (`3.86 MB` saved)—while static media optimization turned a `1.5 MB` diorama PNG into a `~28 KB` WebP fallback.
eli5.audioScript: Have you ever opened a fancy three-D website on your phone and felt the battery get warm while the screen froze? Almost every time, the culprit is an uncompressed three-D model paired with sloppy animation loops. Stage two B fixes both problems cleanly. First, our optimizer runs pure JavaScript compression using Meshopt, quantization, and crisp WebP textures—no finicky native binaries to install. On the GT-Alpaca website, that pipeline shrank the raw Avalon alpaca model from four point five two megabytes all the way down to eight hundred fifty-two kilobytes, saving eighty-one point five seven percent of the file size! Even the fallback diorama picture shrank from one point five megabytes to twenty-eight kilobytes. Finally, our static audit checks every frame loop so older devices stay cool, smooth, and fast.
eli5.diagramCaption: How raw 3D models shrink through Meshopt + WebP compression and pass mobile 60 FPS safety rules before reaching visitors.

keyTakeaways: Verified GT-Alpaca GLB Compression (`03-tokens-and-glb.json`): `4,736,680 B` (`4.52 MB`) -> `872,868 B` (`852 KB`) = **`81.57%` reduction (`3.86 MB` saved)** via `prune -> weld -> KHR_mesh_quantization -> meshopt -> webp 1024px`.

Static Media Budget Verified: Generated `28` WebP assets (`22` herd sculpt renders + `5` studio posters + hero diorama fallback dropping from `1.5 MB` PNG to `~28 KB` WebP), plus `12 MB` `45s` `60fps` trailer and off-by-default `preload=none` ambient audio.

Non-Negotiable R3F / Three.js Invariants: Zero `setState` or `new THREE.*` allocations inside `useFrame`, use `Timer` (never deprecated `THREE.Clock`), clamp DPR `<= 2` with `<PerformanceMonitor>`, cap dynamic lights `<= 3`, and gate `lil-gui`/`stats-gl` to dev only.

Graceful Fallback Guarantee: Always pair `<Canvas>` with a static WebP fallback for `prefers-reduced-motion` and `webglcontextlost`, keeping primary headings and copy in crawlable SSR HTML outside `<canvas>`.
actionChecklist: Compress every raw `.glb` with `optimize-glb.mjs --texture-format webp --max-texture-size 1024` and log the before/after byte JSON.
Configure R3F `<Canvas dpr={[1, 2]}>`, Drei `<PerformanceMonitor>`, `three` `Timer`, and a `prefers-reduced-motion` + `webglcontextlost` static WebP fallback.
Run `audit-threejs.mjs --dir src/` after building 3D components and verify exit code `0`.

codeSnippet.filename: Stage 2B Zero-Native-Binary GLB Compression & Static Audit
codeSnippet.code:
# 1. Compress raw .glb -> Meshopt + KHR_mesh_quantization + WebP 1024px
node skills/cf-threejs-craft/scripts/optimize-glb.mjs \
  --in ../herd_and_co/creative/poc/avalon_poc.glb \
  --out public/models/avalon.glb \
  --texture-format webp \
  --max-texture-size 1024

# 2. Audit R3F/Three.js source for useFrame leaks, Clock, DPR & unguarded lil-gui
node skills/cf-threejs-craft/scripts/audit-threejs.mjs --dir src/

steps.title: Partitioned Swarm Build & Tri-Layer GEO / AEO / SEO (Stage 3)
steps.summary: Build fast without file collisions by partitioning Stage 3 across disjoint Swarm workers (3D & Media, Token UI, and SSR Routes/APIs) while enforcing `cf-geo-seo` invariants: real SSR HTML outside WebGL canvases, AI-permissive `robots.txt` (`GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `PerplexityBot`, `Google-Extended`), connected JSON-LD `@graph`, and 40–60 word AEO answers.

eli5.plainTitle: Build All Five Pages in Parallel So Humans and AI Search Can Read Everything
eli5.oneLineHook: Let three focused builders work side by side while making sure Google, Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude can read every word without guessing.
eli5.everydayAnalogy: A museum where the 3D sculpture stands in the center while clear, well-lit plaques on the wall let every visitor and tour guide quote the exact facts.
eli5.simpleExplanation: Many flashy 3D websites trap all their words inside JavaScript code, which means AI search assistants arrive and see an empty blank box! In Stage three, we split our build into three separate lanes—one for the 3D studio, one for clean buttons and sections, and one for five server-rendered pages. Every headline, stat, and answer lives in plain server HTML, linked together with structured data cards and an open welcome mat for AI crawlers.
eli5.whyItMatters: AI crawlers execute zero JavaScript. If your copy only appears after scripts run, or if your robots file accidentally blocks Google-Extended or GPTBot, your brand becomes invisible in generative search answers.
eli5.roleInProtocol: This combines Stage 3 partitioned Swarm building (`cf-implement`) with Tri-Layer Discovery (`cf-geo-seo` covering traditional SEO, Answer Engine Optimization, and Generative Engine Optimization), verified by `audit-geo-seo.mjs`.
eli5.howToUseGoingForward: Keep all H1s, opening summaries, tables, and 40–60 word FAQ answers in Next.js Server Components, connect entities via one JSON-LD `@graph`, allow `GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `PerplexityBot`, and `Google-Extended` in `robots.ts`, and audit rendered HTML with `audit-geo-seo.mjs`.
eli5.whenToUse: Apply this pattern whenever building marketing hubs, product microsites, or documentation portals that combine rich client interactivity with organic SEO and AI answer-engine discovery.
eli5.realWorldExample: Proof #04 on `gt-alpaca-website` locked 5 SSR hub-and-spoke routes (`/`, `/game`, `/sponsors`, `/farms`, `/faq`), 23 `data-testid` contracts, 8 AEO FAQs (`40–60` words each), connected `FAQPage` + `HowTo` JSON-LD `@graph`, and 2 Zod-validated API routes.
eli5.audioScript: Here is a secret that trips up thousands of modern websites: AI search assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Gemini do not run heavy browser scripts when they scan a page. If all your text lives inside a three-D canvas or slow client code, search bots see a blank screen. Stage three solves both speed and discovery at once. First, we split coding across three non-overlapping workers—one for three-D scenes, one for token-styled sections, and one for server-rendered pages and safe APIs. Second, we render every headline, stat, and forty-to-sixty-word FAQ answer straight from the server in clean HTML, connect every entity with a structured JSON-LD graph, and invite AI crawlers explicitly in robots dot text. On GT-Alpaca, all five hub-and-spoke routes follow this exact contract.

keyTakeaways: Zero-Collision 3-Worker Stage 3 Partition (`cf-implement`): Worker A owns `src/components/three/*` & audio; Worker B owns `src/components/ui/*` & sections; Worker C owns SSR `src/app/**/page.tsx`, `robots.ts`, `sitemap.ts`, `schema-graph.ts`, and Zod API routes.

Verified GT-Alpaca 5-Route Contract (`04-spec-and-feature-map.txt`): `/` (Flagship 3D Hub), `/game` (22 Alpacas, 7 Routes, 22 Songs), `/sponsors` (4 Child-Safe Pillars), `/farms` (White-Label Platform), and `/faq` (8 AEO FAQs + connected JSON-LD `@graph`).

Stateless Zod API Boundary: Locked `GET /api/health` (`200 { status: "ok" }`) and `POST /api/inquiries` (Zod validation, `<= 8 KB` body cap, `202` honeypot, `429` sliding-window rate limit, `maxDuration = 10`).

Tri-Layer Discovery (`cf-geo-seo`): Raw SSR HTML outside `<canvas>`, explicit `robots.txt` allows for `GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `PerplexityBot`, and `Google-Extended`, `<title> <= 60` chars, meta description `140–155` chars, and automated `audit-geo-seo.mjs` verification.

steps.title: Full-Stack Gates & 3-Viewport Feature Map Check (Stage 4A)
steps.summary: Never trust 'it compiled on my machine.' Stage 4A executes deterministic full-stack verification (`cf-next-verify`: TypeScript, ESLint, Vitest coverage, secret/boundary scan, `dependency-cruiser`, and production `next build`) followed by headless 3-viewport `cf-verify-map` sweeps (`375px`, `768px`, `1440px`) checking every route, `data-testid`, HTTP status, console error, and `0px` horizontal overflow.

eli5.plainTitle: Run Every Automated Safety Check Across Phone, Tablet, and Laptop Screens
eli5.oneLineHook: Before asking a human to review your site, let six strict robot inspectors test the code and open every page at three real screen sizes.
eli5.everydayAnalogy: A new car rolling through automated brake, headlight, airbag, and rain-tunnel tests before a human test driver ever grabs the keys.
eli5.simpleExplanation: A website can look fine on a wide desktop monitor while hiding broken buttons, secret leaks, or sideways scrolling on a narrow phone. Stage four A runs two rock-solid automated sweeps. First, our six-part code harness checks types, style rules, unit tests, accidental secrets, clean folder boundaries, and a full production build. Second, our Feature Map robot opens every single route at phone, tablet, and desktop widths to prove zero console errors and zero sideways screen overflow.
eli5.whyItMatters: Automated multi-viewport gates catch real production breaks—like a missing button selector, a broken API route, or a wide table blowing out mobile layouts—in seconds, with repeatable proof every time.
eli5.roleInProtocol: This is Stage 4A (`cf-next-verify` + `cf-verify-map`), generating Proof #06 (`verify-stack.sh` 6/6 output) and Proof #07 (`run-verify-map.mjs --all-viewports` 375px / 768px / 1440px verification matrix).
eli5.howToUseGoingForward: Run `verify-stack.sh` and `run-verify-map.mjs --all-viewports` against a real `next start` production server before every PR or deploy—and update `.memory/feature-map.md` in the same commit whenever routes or `data-testid` selectors change.
eli5.whenToUse: Run Stage 4A right after Stage 3 workers finish synthesizing a milestone, and re-run it after every bug fix before calling the independent reviewer.
eli5.realWorldExample: On `gt-alpaca-website`, Proofs `#06` and `#07` passed `6/6` `verify-stack.sh` gates (`29/29` Vitest `85.64%` lines, `44` `depcruise` modules `0` violations, `11/11` routes) and `15/15` `cf-verify-map` checks across `375px`, `768px`, and `1440px` (`0` errors, `0px` overflow).
eli5.audioScript: Imagine finishing a shiny new car and shipping it straight to buyers without checking the brakes or turning on the headlights in the dark. Stage four A prevents that with two unskippable robot checks. First, our full-stack verification script runs six automated gates in sequence: TypeScript types, ESLint style rules, unit tests, a secret leak scanner, architecture boundary checks, and a real production build. Second, our Feature Map checker boots the production server and opens every single route across three screen widths: a narrow phone at three hundred seventy-five pixels, a tablet at seven hundred sixty-eight pixels, and a desktop at fourteen hundred forty pixels. It checks every button selector, verifies zero browser errors, and confirms zero sideways scrolling before any human reviewer looks at the work.

keyTakeaways: 6-Gate `cf-next-verify` Pipeline (`Proof #06`): Sequentially runs `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, `vitest --coverage`, static secret/boundary scan, `dependency-cruiser` (`0` boundary violations), and production `next build`.

3-Viewport `cf-verify-map` Contract (`Proof #07`): Audits every route in `.memory/feature-map.md` at `375px` (mobile), `768px` (tablet), and `1440px` (desktop) for HTTP `200`, required `data-testid` selectors, `0` console/page/network errors, and `0px` horizontal overflow.

Production Server Fidelity: Always run `cf-verify-map` against `next build && next start`—never rely solely on `next dev`—so production SSR HTML, headers, and image caching behave identically to live hosting.

Verified GT-Alpaca Pass 2 Results: `verify-stack.sh` passed `6/6` (`29/29` Vitest `85.64%` lines, `44` `depcruise` modules `0` violations) and `cf-verify-map` passed `15/15` checks (`375px`/`768px`/`1440px`, `0px` overflow) plus the live Chromium `/farms` -> `POST /api/inquiries` `201` happy path.

steps.title: Decoupled Dual-Axis Evaluation & Answerability (Stage 4B)
steps.summary: Never let the generator grade its own homework. Stage 4B delegates an independent `cf-reviewer` in a clean read-only context to run `cf-eval` and `cf-qa-review` across two axes—Output Quality (security, tokens, 3D, GEO, visual QA) and Execution Trajectory (spec fidelity, zero weakened tests, honest metrics)—producing an Answerability Statement and an explicit `SHIP`, `REVISE`, or `BLOCK` verdict.

eli5.plainTitle: Bring In a Fresh Independent Inspector to Grade Both Result and Honesty
eli5.oneLineHook: Never let the same AI helper that wrote your website also grade its own final exam—hire a fresh inspector who checks both quality and honesty.
eli5.everydayAnalogy: A city building inspector from outside the construction company checking both the finished wiring and the permit logbook before signing off.
eli5.simpleExplanation: Even smart AI builders can develop blind spots—or accidentally take a shortcut like muting a warning just to make a test turn green. That is why Stage four B brings in a brand-new, read-only reviewer who had nothing to do with building the site. The inspector grades two things separately: first, does the finished website actually work, stay safe, and look crisp on every screen? Second, did the builders follow the spec honestly without cheating any checks?
eli5.whyItMatters: Independent dual-axis grading catches subtle security leaks, skipped accessibility checks, and silent test-weakening before real visitors or customers ever encounter them—giving you full confidence to explain why the launch is safe.
eli5.roleInProtocol: This is Stage 4B (`cf-eval` + `cf-qa-review` executed by `cf-reviewer` with read-only tools), writing `.memory/qa-report.md` and Proof #08 (`SHIP` / `REVISE` / `BLOCK` scorecard + Outer-Loop Answerability Statement).
eli5.howToUseGoingForward: Before any staging or production launch, invoke `cf-reviewer` in a clean subagent context against your locked spec and `git diff`, demand both Output Quality and Trajectory scores, and fix every blocking item until it issues an explicit `SHIP`.
eli5.whenToUse: Run decoupled `cf-eval` at the end of every major website milestone, security change, or release candidate—never skip it when deadlines feel tight.
eli5.realWorldExample: On `gt-alpaca-website`, Proof `#08` proved decoupled review works: Pass 1 `cf-reviewer` issued `BLOCK` over dark Espresso text contrast and a Next.js 16 `_global-error.html` edge case, then certified Pass 2 `SHIP` (`0` P0, `0` P1) once both blockers and 4 polish items were closed with regression tests.
eli5.audioScript: Imagine a student writing an exam, grading their own paper, and giving themselves an A plus. Nobody would trust that diploma! Stage four B enforces our favorite engineering rule: never let the builder grade its own homework. Once all automated tests turn green, we spin up a completely fresh, read-only reviewer subagent that never touched the code. That independent inspector grades two distinct axes. Axis one checks Output Quality: security, accessibility contrast, three-D smoothness, search crawlability, and live phone-to-desktop screenshots. Axis two checks Execution Trajectory: did the builders follow the locked spec, stay inside their file partitions, and keep every test honest without sneaking in bypasses? Only an explicit SHIP verdict unlocks human launch approval.
eli5.diagramCaption: How a clean-context cf-reviewer grades Output Quality and Execution Trajectory separately before issuing SHIP, REVISE, or BLOCK.

keyTakeaways: Axis 1 — Output Quality (`cf-qa-review`): Audits all 5 Website Factory gates (`verify-stack`, `validate-tokens`, `audit-threejs`, `audit-geo-seo`, `verify-map`), Zod API boundaries, secret hygiene, and live 3-viewport browser visuals.

Axis 2 — Execution Trajectory (`cf-eval`): Audits spec compliance, disjoint Swarm partition discipline, and anti-gaming oracle honesty (zero weakened assertions, `@ts-ignore`, disabled ESLint rules, or fabricated proof metrics).
Outer-Loop Answerability Statement: Every `SHIP` report documents in plain language what changed, why it is safe, what risks remain, and the exact rollback command.
Clean-Context Separation: `cf-reviewer` operates read-only (`subagent: true`, `mainAgent: false`) so it can never silently patch code to rubber-stamp its own verdict.
actionChecklist: Run all 5 Website Factory automated gates first so `cf-reviewer` inspects verifiable command outputs.
Spawn a fresh `cf-reviewer` subagent (`cf-eval`) with the locked spec path and `git diff` scope.
Archive the `SHIP` scorecard and Answerability Statement to `.memory/qa-report.md` and `proof-pack/08-cf-eval-ship.*`.

eli5.everydayAnalogy: A mission flight director checking every green console light, confirming the abort switch works, giving the final go-ahead, and filing the flight recorder.
eli5.simpleExplanation: Even when every robot check and independent review says SHIP, the Code Factory never silently pushes a site to live customers behind your back. Stage five shows you the release summary and exact undo command, waits for your explicit thumbs-up, deploys the site, and immediately runs fast five-second checks against the live web address—confirming pages, search files, and forms answer cleanly. prompts.title: Orchestrate the Full 6-Stage Vibe Website Factory Pipeline (cf-website-factory)
prompts.eli5Title: Build a Complete 3D & AI-Friendly Website From Brief to Proof Pack 09
prompts.description: Runs the end-to-end 6-stage cf-website-factory workflow from workspace bootstrap, grounded research, and Creative Brief through W3C tokens, GLB compression, Swarm build, 5 automated gates, and Proof Pack 01–09.
prompts.whenToUse: Copy this at the start of any new website or product microsite build to run the entire grounded, accessible, 3D-capable, AI-citable pipeline under Code Factory governance.
prompts.template:
Orchestrate the full 6-stage `cf-website-factory` pipeline for `{{site_name}}` inside `{{workspace_dir}}`:

1. **Stages 0–1 (Bootstrap, Grounded Research & Brief):** Run `cf-bootstrap`, ground all product stats strictly from `{{source_repos}}` (zero fabricated claims), ask me 5 `cf-grill-me` Creative Brief questions, verify 100% MIT/ISC/Apache-2.0 licenses, and pass `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` (`0` High/Critical CVEs). Save Proofs `01` & `02`.
2. **Stage 2 (Spec, Tokens & 3D Prep):** Lock `plans/{{site_slug}}-spec.md` and `.memory/feature-map.md`, compile 3-layer W3C `design/tokens.json` (`>= 4.5:1` WCAG AA), and compress raw `.glb` assets with `optimize-glb.mjs` (Meshopt + WebP 1024px). Save Proofs `03` & `04`.
3. **Stage 3 (Partitioned Swarm):** Execute disjoint workers for 3D/Media, Token UI, and SSR Routes (`{{target_routes}}`) + connected JSON-LD `@graph` + AI-permissive `robots.txt`.
4. **Stages 4–5 (Gates, Eval & HITL Launch):** Pass all 5 Website Factory gates, invoke clean-context `cf-reviewer` (`cf-eval`) for a `SHIP` verdict, assemble numbered Proof Pack `01–09`, and pause at the HITL launch gate with an explicit rollback command.

variables.label: Website / Brand Name
variables.placeholder: e.g., The Herd of Ibiza: GT-Alpaca

variables.label: Primary Source Repos for Grounded Facts

prompts.expectedOutcome: A spec-locked, token-verified, 3D-optimized, AI-citable website backed by numbered Proof Pack 01–09 and an independent cf-reviewer SHIP verdict ready for HITL launch.

prompts.title: Author 3-Layer W3C Design Tokens & Enforce WCAG >= 4.5:1 (cf-design-tokens)
prompts.eli5Title: Create a Smart Color & Spacing System That Auto-Checks Readability
prompts.description: Creates a 3-layer W3C design/tokens.json (primitive, semantic, component + dark overrides), compiles it to Tailwind CSS v4 @theme inline with >= 4.5:1 WCAG AA contrast enforcement, and validates source files against hardcoded literals.
prompts.whenToUse: Copy this before writing any UI styles or components so your entire site shares one accessible, dark-mode-ready token system with zero hardcoded hex hacks.
prompts.template:
Build a token-first design system for `{{brand_aesthetic}}` using `skills/cf-design-tokens/SKILL.md`:

1. Author `{{tokens_path}}` using the strict 3-layer W3C hierarchy: `primitive` (raw palette, typography, spacing, radii), `semantic` (intent-named aliases like `background`, `foreground`, `primary`, `border`, `ring`—never appearance names like `blue-500`), `component` (`button.*`, `card.*`, `badge.*`), and `dark.semantic` overrides.
2. Compile via `node skills/cf-design-tokens/scripts/generate-tokens.mjs --config {{tokens_path}} --out {{css_out_path}} --format tailwind-v4` and fix any contrast pair below `4.5:1` until exit `0`.
3. Scan `{{source_dir}}` via `node skills/cf-design-tokens/scripts/validate-tokens.mjs --dir {{source_dir}}` to confirm zero raw `#hex`, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, or arbitrary Tailwind brackets (`bg-[#...]`, `p-[19px]`).
4. Record exact token layer counts and verified WCAG pair totals for the Proof Pack.

variables.label: Brand Palette Polarity & Aesthetic
variables.placeholder: e.g., Sunlit Ibiza Warm Sand light-first with deep olive ink + dark mode
variables.defaultValue: High-craft editorial light-first palette with accessible dark overrides

prompts.expectedOutcome: A compiled Tailwind CSS v4 tokens.css file with 100% WCAG 2.1 AA >= 4.5:1 verified pairs and a clean validate-tokens.mjs scan showing zero hardcoded literals.

prompts.title: Compress .glb Assets & Build Mobile-Safe R3F 3D Scenes (cf-threejs-craft)
prompts.eli5Title: Shrink Heavy 3D Models & Build a Smooth 60 FPS Mobile-Safe Hero
prompts.description: Compresses raw .glb models via zero-native-binary Meshopt + KHR_mesh_quantization + WebP, implements R3F v9 scenes with PerformanceMonitor, Timer, dev-only lil-gui, and static fallbacks, and passes audit-threejs.mjs.
prompts.whenToUse: Copy this whenever adding an interactive 3D hero or Three.js/R3F canvas so models download fast on mobile, frames stay smooth, and debug panels never leak into production.
prompts.template:
Implement a production 60 FPS 3D web experience for `{{scene_goal}}` following `skills/cf-threejs-craft/SKILL.md`:

1. **Zero-Native-Binary GLB Compression:** Run `node skills/cf-threejs-craft/scripts/optimize-glb.mjs --in {{raw_glb_path}} --out {{out_glb_path}} --texture-format webp --max-texture-size 1024` and log exact before/after bytes and reduction percentage.
2. **Hybrid SSR + Mobile-Safe R3F Scene:** Keep all H1s, copy, and CTAs in crawlable SSR HTML outside `<Canvas>` (`pointer-events: none` on passive overlays). Clamp DPR (`<= 2`), wrap in Drei `<PerformanceMonitor flipflops={3} onFallback={() => setDpr(1)} />`, use `Timer` from `three` (never deprecated `THREE.Clock`), keep dynamic lights `<= 3`, and never call `setState` or allocate `new THREE.*` inside `useFrame`.
3. **Fallbacks & Dev Isolation:** Render a lightweight static WebP fallback (`{{fallback_webp}}`) for `prefers-reduced-motion` and `webglcontextlost`, and gate `lil-gui`/`stats-gl` strictly behind `process.env.NODE_ENV === "development"`.
4. **Static Audit Gate:** Pass `node skills/cf-threejs-craft/scripts/audit-threejs.mjs --dir src/` with exit `0`.

variables.label: 3D Hero or Interactive Scene Description
variables.placeholder: e.g., Interactive Avalon alpaca turntable with soft Mediterranean daylight
variables.defaultValue: Interactive 3D hero turntable with smooth orbit damping and WebP fallback

prompts.expectedOutcome: A dramatically compressed .glb model with logged byte savings, a mobile-safe 60 FPS R3F scene with reduced-motion fallback, and a clean exit-0 audit-threejs.mjs report.

prompts.title: Implement Tri-Layer GEO / AEO / SEO & Connected JSON-LD @graph (cf-geo-seo)
prompts.eli5Title: Make Every Page Easy for Google, Gemini, ChatGPT & Claude to Read and Cite
prompts.description: Builds SSR crawlable hub-and-spoke pages, AI-permissive robots.txt, connected JSON-LD @graph schemas, conclusion-first 40–60 word AEO answers, and passes audit-geo-seo.mjs.
prompts.whenToUse: Copy this when building your website routes, metadata, FAQ pages, and robots.txt so traditional search engines and generative AI answer engines can extract and cite your verified facts.
prompts.template:
Implement Tri-Layer SEO, AEO, and GEO discovery across `{{site_routes}}` for `{{entity_name}}` using `skills/cf-geo-seo/SKILL.md`:

1. **SSR HTML Imperative:** Ensure every H1, 50–150 word opening declarative summary, verified metric table, and 40–60 word FAQ answer renders in raw Server Component HTML outside WebGL canvases.
2. **Permissive AI `robots.txt`:** Explicitly allow `GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `PerplexityBot`, and `Google-Extended` in `src/app/robots.ts` and publish `src/app/sitemap.ts`.
3. **Connected JSON-LD `@graph`:** Emit one connected `@graph` linking `Organization`, `{{primary_schema_type}}`, `WebPage`, `FAQPage`, `HowTo`, and `BreadcrumbList` via stable `@id` IRIs on `{{canonical_origin}}`.
4. **Metadata & Automated Audit:** Enforce `<title> <= 60` chars, meta description `140–155` chars, canonical links, and `html[lang]`, then pass `node skills/cf-geo-seo/scripts/audit-geo-seo.mjs --html .next/server/app --robots public/robots.txt` with exit `0`.

variables.label: Brand / Product Entity Name
variables.placeholder: e.g., The Herd of Ibiza: GT-Alpaca

prompts.expectedOutcome: SSR-crawlable pages with connected JSON-LD @graph schemas, AI-permissive robots.txt, concise AEO answers, and an exit-0 audit-geo-seo.mjs report.

prompts.title: Run All 5 Website Factory Gates, Assemble Proof Pack 01–09 & Run cf-eval
prompts.eli5Title: Run Every Website Quality Gate, Build Proof Pack 01–09 & Get a Fresh SHIP Grade
prompts.description: Executes all 5 deterministic Website Factory gates (verify-stack, validate-tokens, audit-threejs, audit-geo-seo, verify-map across 3 viewports), compiles Proof Pack 01–09 with zero fabricated numbers, and invokes clean-context cf-reviewer (cf-eval).
prompts.whenToUse: Copy this right after building your website (or before staging/production launch) to prove every technical, visual, accessibility, 3D, and AI-discovery gate passes honestly.
prompts.template:
Execute Stage 4 full verification and Proof Pack assembly for `{{project_dir}}` against `{{spec_path}}`:

1. **Run All 5 Deterministic Website Factory Gates:**
   - `bash skills/cf-next-verify/scripts/verify-stack.sh {{project_dir}} --coverage` (`6 passed, 0 failed`)
   - `node skills/cf-design-tokens/scripts/validate-tokens.mjs --dir {{project_dir}}/src`
   - `node skills/cf-threejs-craft/scripts/audit-threejs.mjs --dir {{project_dir}}/src`
   - `node skills/cf-geo-seo/scripts/audit-geo-seo.mjs --html {{project_dir}}/.next/server/app --robots {{project_dir}}/public/robots.txt`
   - `node skills/cf-verify-map/scripts/run-verify-map.mjs --map {{project_dir}}/.memory/feature-map.md --all-viewports` (`375px`, `768px`, `1440px`)
2. **Assemble Honest Proof Pack `01–09`:** Save real command excerpts, byte/contrast JSON, and 3-viewport screenshots under `{{proof_pack_dir}}` (never fabricate pending metrics or missing URLs).
3. **Decoupled Dual-Axis Audit (`cf-eval`):** Invoke read-only `cf-reviewer` in a clean context to grade Output Quality + Execution Trajectory, author an Answerability Statement, write `.memory/qa-report.md`, and issue `SHIP`, `REVISE`, or `BLOCK`.
prompts.expectedOutcome: Verified exit-0 logs across all 5 Website Factory gates, a complete honest Proof Pack 01–09 folder, and an independent cf-reviewer SHIP scorecard in .memory/qa-report.md.
